decisions.reason: An individual finite nondegenerate mesh has some finite maximum h_K/rho_K, which may diverge across meshes. The original each-mesh wording omitted the single family bound defined by def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes and needed for the downstream interpolation constant. The Definition now explicitly requires one sigma for all cells of all meshes; coefficients, domain and solution class are unchanged.

For nonzero endpoint data the nodal set is an affine translate, not a vector subspace: zero need not satisfy the endpoints. Added the precise affine-space terminology and the explicit lifting ell(x)=(1-x)g0+xg1; V_h remains the homogeneous vector space. N=1 gives a singleton affine trial space and zero homogeneous space. Every actual trial set and PDE hypothesis is unchanged.

The original hypotheses admit Omega=R^d, a one-cell constant velocity space, Q_h={0}, sigma=1, beta=f=0; the reaction pairing of that constant with itself is infinite. This is a failure of real bilinear-form well-definedness. Added L2 integrability of velocities, cellwise first derivatives/Laplacians, pressures and cellwise pressure gradients. Bounded coefficients and Cauchy-Schwarz now make every residual, load, mixed, diffusion and grad-div integral finite; finite sums and nonnegative finite parameters cause no additional issue. No boundary or stability claim was added.

F1 attributed arbitrary-partition nodal interpolation to a model defining only a uniform P1 space, and that supplier never defines I_hu. The Statement itself defines the interpolant, so F1 now explicitly derives its affine/nodal properties from that definition; the inaccurate citation contract was removed. The existing proof is sound: averaging u-prime gives a cell derivative error at most h_K times M, integration gives h_K squared times M, and summing h_K fifth powers yields at most h to the fourth. The general partition and bound are preserved.

F3 incorrectly presented the tau and Pe formulas as conclusions of the parameter-bound lemma. The residual-form Definition supplies tau and the model Definition supplies Pe; the facts now say so. F3 correctly records the lemma positivity and step 2.1 uses it to show D>0. Independently recomputed the two-cell equation D(2U-1)/h+b/2=0, D=(bh/2)coth(Pe), U=1/(exp(2Pe)+1), and the exact midpoint match. At x=.99, u_h=.98+.02U tends to .98 while the exponential exact solution tends to zero. The Example is unchanged.

The body and verification correctly use two half-unit cells and one interior hat-function coefficient. Only the title said one-cell; it now says two-cell. Checked the exact solution u=x-(exp(x)-1)/(e-1), u*=1/2-1/(sqrt(e)+1)>0, integral phi squared-gradient=4, integral phi=1/2, zero convection and stabilization load, and U=1/[8(1+M tau)]. Positivity of tau gives U tending to zero and the stated sufficient half-value threshold. The Example and verification are unchanged.
